subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — paging hygiene + escalation thresholds (review by Feb 18)

body:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 16, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Escalation Playbook v2 — paging hygiene + escalation thresholds (review by Feb 18)

Hey Sean,

Sharing the latest draft for v2. We tried to tighten “what constitutes an escalation” + when Support should page SRE/oncall vs keep it in Support Eng / async triage.

Main asks:
- Are the paging thresholds sane (esp. 429/timeout/streaming disconnects)?
- Anything you’d change to reduce alert fatigue without missing true incidents?
- OK with a 30-day pilot where we measure pages vs confirmed incidents + time-to-mitigation?

Attachments:
- Escalation_Playbook_v2_Escalation_Thresholds_draft_2026-02-15.docx
- Escalation_Playbook_v2_SLA_tables_draft_2026-02-15.pdf

If it’s easier I can also hop on a 15 min sync today.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Director, Customer Support
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 16, 2026 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — paging hygiene + escalation thresholds (review by Feb 18)

Dev — thanks. Read through both drafts.

High level: direction is right, but I want us to be stricter on what triggers a page. We’ve made good progress on oncall sanity; this playbook shouldn’t re-open the “page for anything that looks scary” loop.

Key feedback / proposed changes:

1) Split “Escalation” vs “Page SRE” more explicitly
- Escalation: Support escalates to Engineering via the escalation channel / ticket and expects engagement within SLA.
- Page SRE: only when we have credible evidence of active production degradation requiring immediate coordination, or the customer impact is both severe and time-sensitive.

Right now the doc reads like “escalation == page” in a few examples.

2) Add hard paging thresholds for common failure modes
For Hosted API:
- 5xx: page if sustained elevated error rate across multiple orgs/regions OR status-page-worthy event suspected.
- Timeouts: page if we see correlated increase in service-side latency/queueing (not just client-side timeouts).
- Streaming disconnects: page if disconnect rate materially increases AND we can tie it to a region/model/runtime change.
- 429s: should almost never page SRE. Most 429 cases are expected throttling, misconfigured retries, or quota confusion. Escalate to the quota/rate-limit owner asynchronously unless we see widespread misbehavior.

For Dedicated:
- Page if contractual SLO breach is imminent (or already happening) and we need to coordinate mitigation (capacity shift, routing, rollback).
- Otherwise: escalation to Dedicated/SRE queue for investigation during business hours.

For Private:
- Page SRE only if it’s our hosted control plane / shared dependency. Otherwise route to Private Deployments + Security on their escalation paths. (We can help coordinate but shouldn’t take every customer’s IdP incident as oncall.)

3) Require minimum evidence before paging (guardrails)
A page should include at least:
- request IDs (>=3), time window, region, model, customer tier
- what changed (if known): deploy, config, model pin
- whether issue reproduces from Redwood sample client

If those aren’t present, the playbook should recommend: collect info first via incident-bot form, then decide.

4) Pilot period + success metrics
Yes to a 30-day pilot, but we should be explicit on evaluation:
- pages/week (by type)
- % pages that are confirmed incidents
- median time-to-ack + time-to-mitigation
- # of “false pages” (no actionable SRE work) and why

We can tighten the thresholds after 2 weeks if volume spikes.

5) Action items (suggested edits)
- Add a “Paging Hygiene” section with the above thresholds.
- Add a flowchart decision: “Is it multi-tenant / multi-customer? Is there evidence of platform degradation?”
- Link to runbooks (even if initial drafts) for streaming/timeout/429 triage. If a runbook doesn’t exist, we should treat that as a work item rather than defaulting to paging.

I can mark up the doc directly if you want, but the above is the crux.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director of Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 16, 2026 at 11:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — paging hygiene + escalation thresholds (review by Feb 18)

This is super helpful — thank you.

Agree we need to make “escalate” vs “page” crystal clear. We’ve had Support default to page in ambiguous cases (especially streaming), and that’s partly because our runbooks are thin.

Proposed updates based on your notes:
- Add a distinct definition block + decision tree: Escalation (async) vs Page SRE (urgent)
- Insert hard “do not page” guidance for 429 and single-org issues unless there’s evidence of platform-wide impact
- Add a “minimum evidence checklist” that incident-bot will enforce (ties to ENG-2843/ENG-2842)
- Add pilot metrics section and cadence (weekly review with Product Ops)

Question: would you be OK if we define “Page SRE” for Dedicated as:
- P0 Dedicated: page (any time)
- P1 Dedicated: page during business hours; after-hours only if customer is in active outage / SLO breach imminent

Trying to thread the needle between enterprise expectations and not paging 2am for a single-customer latency regression that can be mitigated by routing in the morning.

If you can do quick doc markup that’d be amazing, but I can also incorporate based on the bullets.

— Dev



From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 16, 2026 at 12:04 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — paging hygiene + escalation thresholds (review by Feb 18)

+1 to Sean’s framing. From the CS side, the biggest failure mode is inconsistency: sometimes Support pages immediately, sometimes we wait, and customers experience it as “Redwood is uncoordinated.”

So I’d rather we:
- set conservative paging rules,
- communicate clear investigation/update timelines for escalations that are NOT pages,
- and make sure Support has confident mitigations/runbooks to lean on.

Dev — on Dedicated P1 after-hours: I’m aligned with the “only if active outage / SLO breach imminent” approach. But we need that wording to be consistent with the SLA language the CSMs will cite. If “after-hours coverage” is limited for P1, it should be explicit in the tier table and in the customer comms templates.

Also strongly in favor of the 30-day pilot with metrics; let’s treat the first 2 weeks as an adjustment period and communicate internally that thresholds may change.

Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 16, 2026 at 2:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — paging hygiene + escalation thresholds (review by Feb 18)

Dev — yes, your Dedicated definition is reasonable with one tweak: make “P1 Dedicated after-hours” require BOTH:
- customer-facing impact is ongoing (not a report of a past spike), AND
- we have an identified mitigation that needs immediate SRE action (capacity shift / routing / rollback), not just “we need someone to look.”

Otherwise we should treat it as escalation with comms cadence + next-business-day engineering engagement.

I’ll do doc markup today. Specific edits I’ll add:
- Replace “page SRE” language in the 429 examples with “escalate to quota/rate-limit owner (async)”
- Add an explicit “single customer != incident” note unless the dependency is shared and degraded
- Add a “runbook first” rule for streaming disconnects + timeouts (if the runbook points to a platform issue, then page)

Also, I suggest we add a backstop mechanism:
- If Support escalates but no eng acknowledgment within X minutes for P0/P1, then page.

That gives Support confidence without making the default a page.

— Sean



From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 16, 2026 at 3:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — paging hygiene + escalation thresholds (review by Feb 18)

Perfect — the “both conditions” tweak makes sense, and I like the backstop mechanism.

Next steps I’ll drive:
1) Update playbook language: Escalation vs Page SRE + add paging hygiene section + hard thresholds.
2) Add backstop: if P0/P1 escalation not acknowledged within 15 min (P0) / 30 min (P1), then page.
3) Ensure tier tables + comms templates match the after-hours expectations (I’ll coordinate w/ Jasmine + PM on final wording).
4) Pilot plan: start Mar 2, weekly review metrics w/ Product Ops; adjust thresholds end of week 2.

Sean — thanks in advance for markup. Once you drop it in, I’ll incorporate and circulate for final sign-off.

— Dev
